answer: Latency Inlet Admission** — each new identity must complete a live, randomized network route through an assigned inlet node before it can transact. The route requires sustained two-way timing variance below a threshold at a known network knoll, which parallel clones cannot fake without dedicated physical paths. Each additional identity forces its operator into a fresh spiral of calibration runs, consuming real bandwidth and synchronized clock time per clone. Cost: hours of per-identity route tuning and dedicated link capacity, not money.
